newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Ivory Coast says coffee crop less than 300,000T.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast says coffee crop less than 300,000T.

text.p: Ivory Coast's coffee crop in the October/September 1996/97 season will be less than 300,000 tonnes, Ivorian Commodity Minister Guy-Alain Gauze said on Wednesday.
"It's less than 300,000 tonnes," Gauze told Reuters in an interview. "If the market is thinking 300,000 tonnes, it will be deeply in trouble."
"For this year, we have done a good job. That's all I can say for the time being," the minister, who is with the Ivorian President on an official visit to Singapore, said.

Ivorian coffee exporters have said that green coffee arrivals at its ports have already totalled around 250,000 tonnes by May 9 in the current season against 180,000 tonnes at the same time last year.
But Gauze said the Ivory Coast would still have to weed out bad beans and that this would keep the crop under 300,000 tonnes. --Rene Pastor, Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
